newsitem.title: JAMAICA: U.S. lawyers condemn WTO banana challenge.
newsitem.headline: U.S. lawyers condemn WTO banana challenge.

text.p: KINGSTON, Jamaica, Jan 31, Reuter - The National Bar Association, which represents African-American lawyers and judges, said Friday it had voted to condemn the U.S. government's challenge to end the Caribbean's preferential banana export regime with Europe.
The association's board of governors is meeting in Montego Bay.

The United States had taken a complaint to the World Trade Organization, charging that the European Union's banana import regime discriminates against bananas exported from Latin countries by U.S. firms. The complaint has the backing of Ecuador, Honduras, Guatemala and Mexico.

The WTO's final report on the matter was expected this month but officials say the organization was caught off-guard by the extent of opposition to Washington's efforts, and the report has therefore been delayed.

The association's decision follows a tour of the region by a group led by U.S. Representative Maxine Waters, head of the congressional black caucus, in early December to explore the question of banana exports and their importance to the Caribbean region.
Dr. Beverly Baker-Kelly of the bar association said it is aware of the black caucus' efforts but would have taken up the issue even if the caucus had not.
The association's leadership met this morning with U.S. Embassy officials and has written to U.S. trade ambassador Charlene Barshefsky.
"Short-sighted policies that would undermine the Caribbean economies will create instability, lead to increases in emigration and narcotics trafficking in the region," the letter said.

The resolution echos observations made in December by Waters and a number of Caribbean leaders that any ensuing economic decline could see local farmers turning to marijuana and a rising incidence of cocaine trans-shipment from South America.
The association of African-American barristers is also asking Washington not to enforce the WTO ruling, should that body rule in favor of the United States.

Banana exports account for some two-thirds of total export earnings in the four Windward Island nations of the eastern Caribbean, and is also a significant portion of earnings for Jamaica, Belize and Surinam.
